description: The physical GSP VRAM share as MAME's own m_gsp_vram memory_share, written straight from the share pointer. This is the physical backing store, not a view of it.

share.authority: MAME memory_share pointer: the harddriv_v.cpp STUNRUN-DUMP hook writes from (const uint8_t *)m_gsp_vram.begin() for exactly m_gsp_vram.bytes()

backing_size_proof: SP-338 page 10 labels the silicon 'VRAM Array (16) 64K x 4'; sixteen 64Kx4 chips are 16 x 256 Kbit = 4 Mbit = 512 KiB.
MAME's own share reports share bytes=524288 words=262144 vram_mask=0x003ffff (gsp_share.txt).

The Lua program-space reader that previously produced a 4 MiB image was reading an address-space view; its file size was the span of GSP BIT addresses sampled, not the number of physical bytes behind them.

addressing.note: TMS34010 program-space addresses are BIT addresses, and the space is configured datawidth 16, addrshift 3. One program-space address unit is one bit.
addressing.consequence: A host HSTADR of $FF896040 lands at physical share byte $12C08, NOT $96040. The & 0xFFFFFFF0 aligns to a 16-bit word (two physical bytes); each HSTADR INCW step of 0x10 advances one word, two bytes.
addressing.why_this_fixture_exists: Because of that conversion, an image sampled across GSP bit addresses is not a VRAM image. Any comparison against this file must convert its addresses first.

supersedes.note: Two earlier files lived at this path. Both are program-address-space samples, not physical VRAM, and both are superseded rather than corrected in place.

first.why_not_vram: Those words are the MC68010's reset stack pointer and reset PC, which live in main CPU RAM at address 0, so the file is main RAM under a VRAM name.
first.provenance: none; added in 5b9b13b with no metadata recording how it was produced

second.why_not_vram: A 4194304-byte read of GSP program addresses 0xff800000-0xffffffff is 4 MiB of BIT-address span, and the share behind it is 512 KiB of physical bytes.
second.history: Committed as the '4 MiB share' in 2439e54, on the 4 MiB claim in docs/mc68010-boot-findings.md section 19. That claim is superseded by section 34.

how_to_verify: size must be 524288. The share is 512 KiB; SP-338 and MAME's memory_share both say so independently.
first 8 bytes must NOT be ffffc000 00000216; that is main RAM's reset vector.
cells/tools/verify-oracle-fixture.py checks all of the above.
limitations: This is service-mode frame 600 and includes whatever the GSP has written by then; it is not a frame-48 snapshot.
It is sparse by design: 5058 nonzero bytes of 524288, because the share is mostly untouched self-test area at this point. A dense capture here is a sign of a misconfigured read, not a better one.
The MAME binary is a local instrumented build; the direct-share hook is not a stock-MAME Lua capability.
